sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether maritime law allows punitive damages for a willful denial of maintenance and cure. The seaman claims the company acted in bad faith. The company argues this specific claim does not support such damages.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The seaman wants the Court to allow punitive damages for a willful denial of maintenance and cure.
The company wants the Court to bar punitive damages for this specific maritime claim.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The seaman argues this claim is a general maritime law cause of action that supports punitive damages.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Scalia asked if punitive damages require a finding of guilt that a winning litigant lacks.
Justice Ginsburg asked if courts have a remedy for litigants who abuse the court process with false pleadings.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the financial risk for companies that deny maintenance and cure. It sets the standard for punishing bad faith in maritime employment disputes. It clarifies the scope of punitive damages in general maritime law.
